generated.title: SIX SEVEN… But Make It an EARTHQUAKE! #shorts
generated.description:
Everyone says SIX SEVEN. But what if it's a magnitude?

In this video the SIX SEVEN opening is just a meme about a number, not a real event. The real earthquake: on January 17, 1994, a magnitude 6.7 earthquake struck Northridge, California. According to the USGS, it began as a rupture on a hidden fault, about 17.5 kilometers deep, and it raised the Santa Susana Mountains by as much as 70 centimeters (about 2.3 feet).

The side view of the fault and the mountain is a schematic illustration, not to scale, with the rise exaggerated. It is not data or footage.

Part of the Earthquake Science Explained series. Subscribe to Next Huge Quake for more earthquake science.
